The debug build should now trust the dev server's certificate. I couldn't build or run the app here, so this is unverified until you run the debug build on the emulator.

**Cause:** The debug build calls `https://10.0.2.2:8443/`, which presents the self-signed dev certificate from `dev-ca/shelftap-dev-ca.pem`. Android doesn't trust that certificate, so the TLS handshake fails before any request is sent.

**Fix:** I added three debug-only files, so the release build and its trust store are unchanged:

- `app/src/debug/AndroidManifest.xml` sets `android:networkSecurityConfig` on the application. It is merged into the main manifest only for debug builds.
- `app/src/debug/res/xml/network_security_config.xml` trusts the dev certificate for the domain `10.0.2.2` only.
- `app/src/debug/res/raw/shelftap_dev_ca.pem` is a copy of `dev-ca/shelftap-dev-ca.pem`. I checked that it has the same 19 lines as the original.

I didn't change any Kotlin or Gradle files. `CatalogClient` already uses the debug URL, so it picks up the trust setting with no code change.

**Things to know:**
- If the dev certificate is regenerated, update the copy in `app/src/debug/res/raw/` too. Keeping a second copy is the trade-off for not changing the Gradle config.
- The trust applies only to `10.0.2.2`. If you reach the dev server through another host name, add a `<domain>` entry for it.
- I didn't change `DEV.md`. It may be worth noting there that the debug build trusts the dev CA.
